checks.evidence: Reasoned, plus the 57 own tests including backend-load tests. set_backend runs once, None to backend, and writes backend before background. schedule_speakers reads background: False (before the swap) returns early and only skips a speaker run, with no corruption (audio is not retained while backend is None, and the next schedule picks up). True means backend is already set, so _speaker_step's read of backend is non-None and has .spans. A backend never goes back to None or changes kind. No exception, no lost or corrupt batch found in any order. assign() reads both under the lock, and the hasattr call is outside the lock, so a spans property calling assign cannot deadlock.

notes: 1) The repo test does not fail if only the lock is removed, because it only exercises the ordering of hasattr versus the stores. Without the lock, assign could in principle see the new backend with the old background=False between the two stores, and then call .label on a spans-only backend. I did not reproduce that by timing, and the lock does protect it by reasoning. A test that makes the stores themselves interleave would pin it. 2) stream.py reads background and backend outside the diarizer's lock; judged safe under the one-time None-to-backend swap with the write order backend then background, and relies on that order. 3) Running my scripts through pytest from the main folder picks up the main src first through the pytest pythonpath setting; I ran them from a temp dir to avoid that. 4) tests/test_diarize_real.py is real-marked and deselected, so only its collection ran. The datasets.md claim that it has run rests on the earlier-checked run record.
